fact.thing: TFSA withdrawal added back as contribution room
fact.claim: The CRA says money you take out of your TFSA only comes back as new contribution room in the next calendar year. So a withdrawal made in 2026 gives you that room back on January 1, 2027, and a withdrawal made in early January 2027 has to wait until 2028. In the CRA's own example, Taylor withdraws $4,000 and gets the $4,000 of room back on January 1 of the following year. The main condition: if you put the money back in the same year without enough unused room, the CRA counts it as an over-contribution.

caption:
🐶⛏️ If you pull $4,000 from your TFSA in January, the room waits a year longer.

The CRA only hands that room back on January 1 the next year, so a late December withdrawal gets it back in days. And putting it back the same year can push you over.

plain.what: Hama took $4,000 out of a TFSA, which is a savings account where your money grows without tax. When you take money out, the space to put money back in does not come back right away. The CRA, Canada's tax office, gives that space back on January 1 of the next year.
plain.so_what: If you take that $4,000 out in early January 2027, the $4,000 of space waits until 2028 — almost a full extra year of waiting.
plain.do: Write down two things today: what year it is, and how much unused room your TFSA has.
